title: alerts for SKIPPED sessions (overlap-lost, untrusted-sender, no-join-link) cannot be resolved by lkb alert-who: skipped items are never persisted locally
evidence: schedule-state.json holds only sessions that were scheduled (recordScheduled); scheduled/*.json only scheduled jobs; operations.json only webinar-release rows. runScheduleTickOnce logs result.skipped and writes nothing. So an overlap-lost / untrusted-sender / join-link alert id has no local row to match; the CLI says so on a miss.
fix_direction: The wiring unit that sends alerts should persist a small id-to-(title,start,platform) record for each alert it sends, in the same tenant state dir, mode 0600, or lkb alert-who should accept a re-run of selectAutoRecordItems over the live calendar. Out of scope here (no sender, no scheduler change).

title: alertIdFor is an unsalted SHA-256 of a session key that is low-entropy for webinar sessions: an alert holder can brute-force the meeting URL offline
evidence: Session keys are cal:<Google event id> (high entropy, about 26 base32 chars), gmail:<Mongo ObjectId> (24 hex; 4-byte timestamp + per-process random + counter, partly guessable), and webinar-<first 24 hex of sha256(identity)> where identity = https URL with only tk/token/access_token/pwd/password/utm_* removed, plus '|' and the ISO start time. The start time is printed in the alert and a Zoom meeting id is 9-11 digits, so the candidate space for a Zoom webinar is about 1e10-1e11 URLs: feasible offline (two chained SHA-256). A passcode under any other parameter name stays in the identity, which adds entropy but makes the hash a verification oracle for a guessed full URL. The recovered value is the meeting URL/id, not a stripped passcode.
fix_direction: HMAC-SHA-256 over the session key with a per-tenant secret kept in the tenant state dir (not in the alert), truncated the same way. This changes every existing alert id, so it is a contract matter for the checker and the Approver; alertIdFor was deliberately NOT changed here. lkb alert-who would then need the same secret, which it has locally.
